residue.item: A large following
residue.why: shadows 'the audience that trusts the voice'; size is not the invariant

residue.item: Patents
residue.why: valuable only inside the objective that motivated them — fails the total-change test

residue.item: Momentum
residue.why: dies with the objective by definition

gaps: The current list emphasizes money, people, standing, capacity, and adaptability; actual disencumbrance and repurposing mechanisms are thin.
Breath one exposes the next gaps: movable, lawful assets may remain unusable because operating limits are unknown or dormancy ruins the substrate.
Operational bridges do not themselves confer mission-changing authority or preserve a scarce future place.
gate: list-excellences; open conceptual or phenomenological hypotheses

accepted.item: The exit clause with a priced release from the old obligation
accepted.why: Short commitments reduce duration; an exercisable exit clause permits departure before duration ends. Its price must remain affordable and its terms enforceable.

accepted.item: The release that leaves no old counterparty with a veto over the next use
accepted.why: A concluded release removes a surviving claim; unlike an exit clause, it is an already-held clearance rather than a future departure option. It is not general legal good standing.

accepted.item: The reuse rights that travel with the material rather than with its first purpose
accepted.why: Possession, an archive, and experimental permission do not grant repurposing rights. Rights must cover the proposed use and relevant recipients.

accepted.item: The source material kept before the first irreversible reduction
accepted.why: Raw observations, masters, or stock preserve transformations discarded by an old-purpose summary. An archive can be retrievable yet contain only reduced outputs.

accepted.item: The working state that can be restored without reconstructing its history
accepted.why: A restorable checkpoint preserves an executable or operational condition; provenance archives preserve knowledge about prior work but need not restore it.

accepted.item: The joints that let a useful part come out without breaking its neighbors
accepted.why: Physical or logical separability preserves extraction value. Standard interfaces govern replacement compatibility, not whether removal destroys adjacent parts.

accepted.item: The repair access left open after assembly
accepted.why: Accessible fastenings, service ports, or replaceable internals keep correction possible. A separable module can still be sealed and unrepairable within itself.

accepted.item: The mission assumptions kept outside the machinery that executes them
accepted.why: Replaceable policy tables, recipes, or parameters allow a retained mechanism to take a new purpose without being rewritten. This is purpose separation, not merely standard connectors.

accepted.item: The identifiers that remain resolvable after the undertaking changes its name
accepted.why: Continuity of references prevents work, obligations, and records from becoming orphaned. This is addressability, not reputation or freedom to own a name.

accepted.item: The bridge that lets old and new operations coexist during transfer
accepted.why: A dual-running adapter or temporary shared service permits incremental handover while obligations continue. It need not be a permanent standard or a rollback checkpoint.

residue.item: The cash that has not yet chosen a purpose
residue.why: Restates the reserve of unallocated capital.

residue.item: The people who can learn a second trade
residue.why: Restates the bench, trained hands, and learning speed without identifying a new retained mechanism.

residue.item: The trust that survives a change of story
residue.why: Rephrases recognized judgment, promise-keeping, and topic-independent audience trust; no further mechanism.

residue.item: The courage to leave the old plan
residue.why: An injunction or disposition, not a sufficiently identifiable retained asset in this register.

residue.item: The universal socket into which any future fits
residue.why: Impossible interface universality; the repaired standard-interface item already captures conditional compatibility.

residue.item: The small promise that never becomes a chain
residue.why: Poetic restatement of short commitments; even short promises can impose costly liabilities.

residue.item: The spare machine waiting for its second life
residue.why: Unused capacity alone is domain-specific inventory; without a distinct transfer mechanism it redescribes reserves and toolchain.

residue.item: The patent freed from its first business case
residue.why: Earlier residue rejected patents too absolutely, but under the repaired universe their useful mechanism is reusable rights or alienable property, already covered; no separate keep.

residue.item: The following large enough to change subjects
residue.why: Earlier residue correctly separates audience size from transferable trust; size adds no distinct mechanism.

residue.item: The momentum that survives the turn
residue.why: Some routines persist, so earlier residue overstated that momentum always dies; the candidate still conflates throughput, habit, and demand rather than naming a transfer asset.

limits: Two authored breaths and one independent model gate, not empirical validation or a world novelty search.
Keep rate covers enumerated growth candidates; any extra repair-origin admissions are recorded separately.

gaps: From the enriched list: compatibility must be knowable, instruments recalibratable, dormant substrates intact, and method changes comparable.
From the enriched list: authority to change purpose, reserved opportunities, and containment of surviving liabilities are distinct from experimental permission and departure rights.
No differentiated category survived for generic spare capacity, reserves, instructions, or metaphorical permission.
Identity rupture, institutional collapse, and harmful repurposing remain transfer failures, not gaps cured by adding nominal assets.
gate: list-excellences; open conceptual or phenomenological hypotheses

accepted.item: The operating limits recorded beside the parts that may be reused
accepted.why: Ratings, tolerances, and excluded conditions make it possible to distinguish a fit from a dangerous analogy. These are transfer constraints, not a general archive or a sensor reading.

accepted.item: The reference standard that can recalibrate the instrument after it moves
accepted.why: A retained reference lets a relocated sensor recover comparable meaning. Reality-directed sensors can still drift; archived readings cannot alone establish a current scale.

accepted.item: The preservation state from which idle equipment can be recommissioned
accepted.why: Protected, maintained dormancy prevents latent deterioration while purpose is undecided. This differs from a checkpoint, which records a recoverable state but does not keep the substrate serviceable.

accepted.item: The reserved place whose use can be chosen later
accepted.why: An enforceable reservation of a scarce slot, site, or allocation preserves access through a decision interval. It is not free cash, a short obligation, or standing access: the scarce opportunity could disappear before purchase.

accepted.item: The authority to amend the mission without dissolving the undertaking
accepted.why: A charter amendment power or equivalent governance authority preserves the continuing entity through a purpose change. Permission to experiment does not authorize a new mission, and reuse rights concern assets rather than governance.

accepted.item: The boundary that keeps an old venture’s liabilities from attaching to the new one
accepted.why: An effective ring-fence limits propagation of existing exposure while that exposure remains. A release extinguishes a claim; clean legal standing can coexist with lawful liabilities. Protection depends on applicable law and actual separation.

accepted.item: The dependency map that marks what else stops when a component is removed
accepted.why: A current dependency map makes collateral loss legible before extraction. Separable joints supply the ability to remove; the map identifies what relies on the removed part. An archive of past work need not describe live dependencies.

accepted.item: The stable reference specimens that let a new method be compared with the old
accepted.why: Retained specimens or cases permit paired comparison across changed procedures. A calibration standard fixes a measurement scale; reference specimens expose changed treatment of the same varied inputs. They need not predict the new objective’s success.

residue.item: The instruction book that can outlive its author
residue.why: Potentially useful, but the retrievable archive and trained hands already admit this; no distinct repurposing mechanism as phrased.

residue.item: The spare parts that keep the old tool alive
residue.why: Inventory instance of toolchain and repairability, not an additional conceptual joint.

residue.item: The cash assigned to closing down
residue.why: Earmarking the existing reserve does not create a new asset type; genuine closure claims belong to exit and release mechanisms.

residue.item: The address that forwards after the old name disappears
residue.why: An instance of resolvable identifiers accepted in breath one.

residue.item: The permission to pause without forfeiting the place
residue.why: Falls within the reserved-place mechanism; do not double-count preservation of the same claim over a decision interval.

residue.item: The shell that can be sold after the contents change
residue.why: Generic resale value returns to fungible capital unless a distinct transfer right is specified; reusable rights already name that distinction.

residue.item: The universal fixture that accepts tomorrow’s work
residue.why: Universal compatibility repeats the original interface overclaim; conditional standard interfaces already survive.

residue.item: The unpainted room that has not been told its purpose
residue.why: Concrete but underspecified: vacant space is not neutral if zoning, load limits, or access prevent reuse. Separability and recorded operating limits state the useful mechanisms.

residue.item: The old obligations kept visible in a ledger
residue.why: A useful instance of the retrievable archive; neither visibility nor recording discharges an obligation or grants an exit.

residue.item: The clean material that has not been contaminated by its first use
residue.why: A physical instance of retaining material before irreversible reduction, already accepted in breath one; contamination resistance could be a design property, but this phrasing only states preserved reuse condition.

residue.item: The team’s permission to become someone else
residue.why: Metaphorical and conflates social acceptance with formal mission-amendment authority; recognized trust and governance authority are the sharper categories.

residue.item: The memory of why the old objective failed
residue.why: A particular content of provenance-bearing prior work, and the record of prior pivots already covers experience; not a third memory asset.

limits: Two authored breaths and one independent model gate, not empirical validation or a world novelty search.
Keep rate covers enumerated growth candidates; any extra repair-origin admissions are recorded separately.

dispositions.before: a strategic asset that remains valuable across a total change in objective
dispositions.proposed: a retained asset that can lower the cost of leaving, restarting, or repurposing an undertaking when its objective changes within a specified transfer envelope
dispositions.why: No asset is valuable under every conceivable objective and environment; conditional transfer replaces universal invariance.

dispositions.proposed: The income-producing asset whose operation does not depend on the abandoned project
dispositions.why: Substitution, not repair: compounding-while-ignored (silent growth through the distraction of the pivot) is a different mechanism from independent income (runway), and the replacement collides with existing neighbors (unallocated reserve, cheapness of staying alive). 'Left alone' already encodes the operational independence the repairer wanted; no overclaim in the original.

dispositions.before: Trust of the kind that transfers without explanation
dispositions.proposed: Trust in judgment that the new counterparties already recognize
dispositions.why: 'Of the kind that' is self-scoping — it names the transferable kind, claiming nothing universal. The replacement swaps the mechanism (portability without re-justification → pre-existing recognition) and overlaps 'The name that opens doors it has never knocked on', reducing differentiation.

dispositions.before: Clean standing before every court that might matter
dispositions.proposed: Clean legal standing in the jurisdictions the new undertaking must use
dispositions.why: 'Might matter' bounds the quantifier; the point is option value of clean standing under ex-ante ignorance of which jurisdictions the next venture needs. 'Must use' presumes the destination is known and deletes that mechanism.

dispositions.before: Interfaces kept standard, so anything modular can be repointed
dispositions.proposed: Standard interfaces shared by the old components and the proposed replacements
dispositions.why: Standards only help when both sides actually share them.

dispositions.before: The distribution channel that carries any cargo
dispositions.proposed: The distribution channel with room for the new offering under its existing rules
dispositions.why: Cargo and access rules constrain portability.

dispositions.before: Position astride a flow — flows change cargo, not geometry
dispositions.proposed: Position astride a flow the new objective still needs to reach
dispositions.why: Flows and geometry can change; relevant retained access is the asset.

dispositions.before: The complete archive of everything already done
dispositions.proposed: The retrievable archive of prior work and its provenance
dispositions.why: Findability and origin, not impossible completeness, support reuse.
